q: Does a group captive solar PPA let me report lower market-based Scope 2?
title: Group captive PPA and market-based Scope 2
short: Yes, but only for the solar units adjusted against your load whose renewable attributes the PPA gives to you alone. Captive status under the Electricity Rules saves surcharges; it does not by itself prove a carbon claim. If RECs or credits were sold for the same units, or the contract is silent, those units take the grid factor.
audience: Indian manufacturers signing open-access or group captive PPAs

sections.h: Captive status and the carbon claim are two separate tests
p: Rule 3 of the Electricity Rules, 2005 decides whether a plant is captive: users holding at least 26% of the equity and consuming at least 51% of the output. Passing it removes the cross subsidy surcharge. The GHG Protocol Scope 2 Quality Criteria decide whether you can use the power to lower market-based Scope 2. A plant can pass the first and fail the second, for example if the attributes were sold to someone else. A group captive plant need not be renewable either, so confirm the source.

ol: Attributes: the PPA or shareholder agreement says the renewable attributes of the units supplied pass to you, and the generator will not sell or claim them elsewhere.
No RECs for your units: the generator has not been issued RECs for the same MWh under the CERC REC Regulations, 2022, or, if it has, you hold and redeem them.
No double claim through credits: if the plant sells carbon credits for the same generation, many buyers and programmes treat the attribute as already used. Ask, and get it in writing.
Units and period: you claim units adjusted at your meter in the reporting year, from the load despatch centre energy account, after losses. Lapsed banked units are out.
Same market: the plant is on India's grid. Indian plants are generally treated as one market for Indian load.

p: Claim zero for a unit only if all five checks pass for it. Units that fail any check stay in market-based Scope 2 at the grid average, 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, disclosed as a proxy because India publishes no residual mix. Location-based Scope 2 stays at total consumption times the grid factor whatever the PPA says.

The GHG Protocol is revising its Scope 2 Guidance. Proposals under discussion include hourly matching of renewable supply to consumption and tighter deliverability rules. A solar PPA that covers your annual units may cover far fewer once matched hour by hour, because solar does not generate at night. If you are signing a long PPA now, ask for hourly generation data in the contract so you can recalculate later.

example.title: Worked example: part of the solar fails the REC check
lines: Annual consumption 3,000 MWh; group captive solar adjusted at the meter 2,000 MWh
The generator sold RECs for 500 MWh of that solar, so only 1,500 MWh pass
Location-based: 3,000 MWh x 0.710 t CO2 per MWh = 2,130 t CO2
Market-based: 1,500 MWh at zero; (3,000 minus 1,500) x 0.710 = 1,065 t CO2
If all 2,000 MWh had passed: 1,000 x 0.710 = 710 t CO2
example.note: Illustrative figures. The test applies unit by unit, so one clause in the PPA can move hundreds of tonnes.

senseible: Senseible reports location-based Scope 2 from your bills at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh and market-based Scope 2 when you supply the PPA, energy account or REC data. It does not test captive compliance or check whether the generator sold RECs or credits for your units.
